title: Vahlen–Capelli Criterion for Binomial Irreducibility Xⁿ − a
description: Generalizes the Eisenstein proof that X³−3 is irreducible over ℚ to the classical Vahlen–Capelli criterion: Xⁿ − a is irreducible over a field K iff (1) a is not a p-th power for any prime p ∣ n, and (2) if 4 ∣ n then a ∉ −4·K⁴. Proves the full odd-n case (via Mathlib's KummerExtension), both necessity obstructions unconditionally (the p-th-power divisor and the Sophie Germain / −4b⁴ factorization), and isolates the even-sufficiency direction — an explicit open TODO in Mathlib — as the sole sorry.

overview.historicalContext: The irreducibility of a binomial Xⁿ − a over a field is one of the oldest questions in the theory of equations. Abel and Galois needed the special case (a a non-residue, n prime) for the theory of radical extensions. The complete answer for all n is due to **K. Th. Vahlen** (1895) and, independently and more fully, to **Alfredo Capelli** (1897): Xⁿ − a is irreducible over K exactly when a is not a p-th power in K for any prime p dividing n, with one extra exception when 4 ∣ n — a must additionally not lie in −4·K⁴. The −4 exception is the algebraic shadow of the **Sophie Germain identity** a⁴ + 4b⁴ = (a²−2ab+2b²)(a²+2ab+2b²) (Germain, ~1825), the smallest Aurifeuillian factorization. The modern textbook reference is Lang, *Algebra*, Chapter VI §9 (Theorem 9.1). In Mathlib, the odd and odd-prime-power cases are formalized in FieldTheory/KummerExtension.lean, but the even case is left as two explicit `TODO`s — the gap this entry targets.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question OQ-03 from cube-root-3-irrational-oq-02.** The parent entry proves ∛3 irrational by showing X³−3 is irreducible over ℚ via Eisenstein at p=3 — the concrete n=3, odd-prime case. The natural generalization is the full Vahlen–Capelli criterion for arbitrary exponent n and radicand a over any field K:

Xⁿ − C a is irreducible over K  ⟺  (1) ∀ prime p ∣ n, a is not a p-th power in K, AND (2) 4 ∣ n ⟹ a ∉ −4·K⁴.

Mathlib supplies the odd case; the even case (condition (2) and its sufficiency) is the open part.
overview.proofStrategy:
The criterion is packaged as a predicate `VahlenCapelliCond K n a`. The file establishes:

**Necessity (both directions, all n, unconditional).** If condition (1) fails — a = cᵖ for a prime p ∣ n=pm — then `obstruction_pow_dvd` gives X^m − C c ∣ Xⁿ − C a via the elementary x−y ∣ xⁿ−yⁿ divisibility, a proper (degree m, 0<m<n) divisor. If condition (2) fails — 4 ∣ n=4m and a = −4b⁴ — then `capelli_factor_dvd`, built on the `sophie_germain` identity with u=X^m, v=C b, exhibits X^{4m} − C(−4b⁴) = X^{4m}+4(C b)⁴ as a product of two degree-2m factors. Either way the binomial is reducible; contrapositively, irreducibility forces both conditions.

**Sufficiency, odd n (complete).** `vahlen_capelli_odd` rewrites via Mathlib's `X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_iff_forall_prime_of_odd` and observes condition (2) is vacuous for odd n (4 ∤ n).

**Sufficiency, even n (the gap).** Reduce n = 2^k·t (t odd): the odd part is handled by the odd theorem after X ↦ X^{2^k}; multiplicativity of binomial irreducibility under coprime exponent factorizations reduces to n = 2^k, then induction on k where the sole obstruction is exactly the −4b⁴ factorization ruled out by condition (2). This is the hard Capelli theorem, left as the single `sorry`.
keyInsights: The entire −4·K⁴ exception in Vahlen–Capelli descends from ONE polynomial identity — Sophie Germain's a⁴+4b⁴ factorization — which is why condition (2) only appears when 4 ∣ n: you need a fourth power of X^m to complete the u⁴ pattern.

Necessity of BOTH conditions is completely elementary and field-agnostic: it needs only x−y ∣ xⁿ−yⁿ (for the p-th-power obstruction) and a `ring` identity (for the −4 obstruction). No Galois theory, no KummerExtension machinery. This cleanly separates the easy half of the criterion from the hard sufficiency half.

Mathlib already draws exactly this odd/even line: `X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_odd` carries a literal `-- TODO: generalize to even n` and `X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime_pow` a `-- TODO: generalize to p = 2`. The even sufficiency isolated here is precisely those two TODOs, so closing this sorry would be an upstreamable Mathlib contribution.

The proper-divisor witnesses are stated as `Dvd` facts rather than degree computations, which keeps the necessity proofs to a single `ring`/`sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow` line each and defers the (routine) 'degree strictly between 0 and n' bookkeeping to the reducibility corollary.
